title: Pioneer Fragment
subtitle: Orphaned slab fragment beneath Oregon
description: A detached piece of the Farallon plate discovered beneath central Oregon at ~200-400 km depth. This 'orphan' fragment provides evidence that slab tearing has shaped the subduction zone's geometry over millions of years.

paper.title: Rayleigh wave tomography of the Cascadia subduction zone

title: Siletzia Terrane Boundary
subtitle: Accreted oceanic plateau affecting plate coupling
description: Siletzia is a large igneous province accreted to North America ~50 Ma. Its dense, rigid basaltic crust creates a sharp rheological boundary that influences megathrust coupling, segmenting the subduction zone and affecting rupture behavior.

paper.title: Segmentation of the Cascadia subduction zone by Siletzia

title: Slab Gap at Cape Mendocino
subtitle: Southern edge tear in the subducting plate
description: At the Mendocino Triple Junction, the southern terminus of Cascadia subduction, a slab gap or tear has been imaged where the Gorda plate meets the transform boundary. This gap allows asthenospheric flow and influences volcanism in northern California.

paper.title: Slab fragmentation and edge flow: implications for the origin of the Yellowstone hotspot track

title: Deep Fluid Pathways
subtitle: Serpentinization and fluid release beneath the Olympics
description: Seismic studies reveal low-velocity zones beneath the Olympic Peninsula interpreted as serpentinized mantle wedge. Water released from the subducting slab transforms mantle peridotite into serpentinite, weakening the plate interface and triggering episodic tremor.

title: Episodic Tremor and Slip Zone
subtitle: Slow slip and non-volcanic tremor on the megathrust
description: Every ~14 months, the Cascadia megathrust experiences slow-slip events accompanied by non-volcanic tremor at 25-45 km depth. These ETS events occur downdip of the locked seismogenic zone and release stress equivalent to a M6.5+ earthquake over weeks.

paper.title: Episodic tremor and slip on the Cascadia subduction zone

title: Gorda Plate Deformation
subtitle: Internal deformation of the youngest oceanic plate
description: The small Gorda plate, south of the Blanco Fracture Zone, undergoes intense internal deformation due to compression between the Pacific and North American plates. This produces frequent intraplate earthquakes and complicates hazard assessment for northern California and southern Oregon.

title: Blanco Fracture Zone
subtitle: Transform fault separating Juan de Fuca and Gorda plates
description: The Blanco Fracture Zone is a ~350 km long right-lateral transform fault connecting the Juan de Fuca and Gorda ridges. It produces frequent M5-6 earthquakes and acts as a structural boundary that may limit southward rupture propagation during great Cascadia earthquakes.

paper.title: Along-strike variations in fault frictional properties along the Blanco Transform Fault
